question.text: A client has a 3-year horizon to buy a house and has a capital-preservation objective. The appropriate SAA, in line with the workbook, is:

answer.text: An allocation tilted toward safe bonds and debt securities, with attention to liquidity needs

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook ties capital preservation to tilting allocation toward safe bonds and debt securities. SAA must follow the investor's goals, risk preferences, and liquidity needs, all of which favour a debt-heavy mix for a near-term goal. The Trap: A 100% equity, derivatives-only, or illiquid private-equity allocation conflicts with capital preservation and the short horizon to a specific goal. Note: Per NISM-XXI-B workbook (p.166 and p.174).
